name: Valparaíso
facts: A Pacific port built across steep hills.
Historic funiculars connect its upper and lower streets.
Chile’s national congress meets here.
photoAlt: A steep hillside port, with colourful houses, historic buildings and a blue Pacific bay.

name: Dubrovnik
facts: A walled city on the Adriatic Sea.
It was the centre of the Republic of Ragusa.
Its old town stood in for King’s Landing on television.
photoAlt: A compact walled coastal city with red tile roofs on a rocky peninsula beside deep blue water.

name: Chefchaouen
facts: A city in the Rif Mountains.
Its old town is famous for blue-painted walls.
It lies in northern Morocco, inland from the Mediterranean.
photoAlt: A blue-painted town beneath steep, dry mountains, with a slender mosque tower.

name: Luang Prabang
facts: The Mekong and Nam Khan rivers meet here.
It was a royal capital of Laos.
Its historic town combines Buddhist temples and colonial architecture.
photoAlt: A green river valley with red-roofed buildings and temple roofs, surrounded by forested mountains.

name: Quebec City
facts: A fortified city above the Saint Lawrence River.
French is the main language of its surrounding province.
The Château Frontenac dominates its skyline.
photoAlt: A broad river below a North American city, with a large copper-roofed château on a bluff.

name: Hobart
facts: A harbour city on the River Derwent.
Kunanyi / Mount Wellington rises behind it.
It is the capital of Tasmania.
artist:
File:Franklin Wharf 2015.jpg: Michael fromholtz
derivative work: Georgfotoart
photoAlt: A marina full of sailing boats beside a low city and a large wooded mountain.

name: Cusco
facts: An Andean city more than 3,000 metres above sea level.
It was the capital of the Inca Empire.
Many travellers start journeys to Machu Picchu here.
photoAlt: A narrow cobbled street with white plaster walls, tiled roofs, heavy stone foundations and a church tower.

name: Bergen
facts: A rainy harbour city on Norway’s west coast.
Its Bryggen wharf was a Hanseatic trading centre.
A funicular climbs from the centre to Mount Fløyen.
photoAlt: A harbour city at dusk, with mountain slopes, islands and waterfront lights.

name: Jaipur
facts: A planned city in Rajasthan.
Its historic centre is known as the Pink City.
The Hawa Mahal has a façade filled with small windows.
photoAlt: A tall pink sandstone façade with many small projecting windows, decorative arches and domed finials.

name: Zanzibar City
facts: A city on the island of Unguja.
Its historic centre is called Stone Town.
It was a major Indian Ocean spice-trading port.
photoAlt: A densely built tropical port with flat-roofed buildings, a projecting waterfront and boats in turquoise water.

name: Guanajuato
facts: A colourful city in Mexico’s central highlands.
Silver mining helped build its wealth.
Road tunnels run beneath its historic centre.
photoAlt: A dense valley city with brightly painted buildings, domed churches and dry green hills.

name: Gjirokastër
facts: A stone-roofed hillside city in the Balkans.
A large fortress overlooks the Drino valley.
Its Ottoman-era houses form a UNESCO site in southern Albania.
photoAlt: A steep cobbled street between pale stone buildings with thick grey roofs, below green mountains.

name: Lüderitz
facts: An Atlantic port beside the Namib Desert.
German colonial buildings line its streets.
The abandoned diamond town of Kolmanskop is nearby.
photoAlt: A dry coastal town with colourful colonial buildings, a church on bare rock and an Atlantic harbour.

name: Khiva
facts: An oasis city in Central Asia.
Its walled inner town is called Itchan Kala.
The unfinished Kalta Minor minaret is covered in turquoise tiles.
photoAlt: A walled desert city with sand-coloured buildings, blue domes and a tall tiled minaret.

name: Sucre
facts: An Andean city known for white colonial buildings.
It is Bolivia’s constitutional capital.
The Casa de la Libertad hosted the declaration of independence.
photoAlt: A highland city of white buildings and red tile roofs, with church towers and mountains in the distance.

name: Ouro Preto
facts: A steep city in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais.
A gold rush financed its elaborate Baroque churches.
Its name translates as Black Gold.
photoAlt: A steep historic town with red tile roofs, white Baroque churches and rounded rocky hills.

name: Kotor
facts: A fortified town deep inside an Adriatic bay.
Its walls climb a steep mountain behind the old town.
It lies in Montenegro, beneath the Lovćen massif.
photoAlt: A red-roofed town and stone church tower beside a narrow blue bay enclosed by steep mountains.

name: Ålesund
facts: A Norwegian coastal city spread over several islands.
It was rebuilt after a devastating fire in 1904.
Its centre is famous for Art Nouveau architecture.
photoAlt: A compact city spread across rocky coastal islands, with multicoloured buildings and distant mountains.

name: Galle
facts: A fortified port on the Indian Ocean.
Portuguese and Dutch rule shaped its coastal fort.
It lies near Sri Lanka’s southwestern tip.
photoAlt: A fortified tropical coastal peninsula, with red tile roofs, trees and waves breaking along the walls.

name: Saint-Louis
facts: A city near the mouth of the Senegal River.
Its historic centre occupies a narrow river island.
The Faidherbe Bridge links the island to the mainland.
photoAlt: A low riverfront town with colonial façades and a slender mosque tower, seen across a wide river.

name: Ushuaia
facts: A port on the Beagle Channel.
It lies on the Argentine side of Tierra del Fuego.
Many Antarctic cruises depart from here.
photoAlt: A port below rugged mountains, with brightly coloured roofs beside a cold, sheltered channel.

name: Dunedin
facts: A city at the head of Otago Harbour.
Its name comes from the Gaelic name for Edinburgh.
It is home to New Zealand’s University of Otago.
photoAlt: A stone railway station tower with an ornate pale clock face and dark masonry under a blue sky.

name: Antsirabe
facts: A highland city on the island of Madagascar.
It is known for thermal springs and colourful rickshaws.
It lies south of Antananarivo, on the route toward Fianarantsoa.
photoAlt: A sunny highland street with colourful two-storey buildings, a decorated tower and hand-pulled rickshaws.
